one direction of [Zel80, Theorem 9.7]. multi (LanglandsMultisegments): uniqueness of the multisegment of a Langlands quotient, and the quotient of m + n is a subquotient of the product; same [Zel80, Section 9; Sil78]. exh (LanglandsExhaustionGL): every irreducible representation is the Langlands quotient of a multisegment; same [Zel80; Sil78]. llc (UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.RecTExists): the statement of Theorem gal-llc-exists; related only in name to the local Langlands correspondence [HT01; Hen00; Sch13] (Chapter galois-representations). conv (LocalConverseGL): cuspidal pi_1, pi_2 of GL_{m+1}(k) such that for every irreducible tau of GL_m(k) the two Rankin-Selberg functional equations at the centre (HasPairEps, with Whittaker functionals and invariant integrals) have the same constant are isomorphic. Related to Henniart's local converse theorem [Hen93] with the functional equation of [JPSS83]; the form differs (twists by GL_{n-1} only, the constant at the centre for each tau) and we have not checked whether it follows from [Hen93] directly. dzi (DepthZeroInduction): if the cuspidal support has depth zero, so does the representation; same [MP94; MP96]. brauer (BrauerDegreeZero): every virtual character of degree zero of a finite group is an integral combination of Ind_H chi - Ind_H 1 with chi a linear character of a subgroup H; a consequence of Brauer's induction theorem [Bra47]. chev (ChevalleyUnits): for m, b > 0 there is a > 0 prime to b such that every unit congruent to 1 mod a is an m-th power; Chevalley's theorem [Che51], with the modulus prime to a given b, which is not part of the statement in [Che51]. litN.aut (GlobalAutomorphicGaloisHypotheses'): decay, hc, fin, js, coh, art, ray, chA and berger as above. cusp (CuspidalSpectrumGL): the cuspidal spectrum of GL_a over a totally complex field decomposes discretely, each irreducible summand has a cuspidal automorphic representation as its K-finite part, and cusp forms invariant under the split centre are bounded; same [GGPS69; MW95, Chapter I]. bc (BaseChangeIsobaricTransfer): Theorem gal-base-change-definite [Lab11]. gk (GelfandKazhdanDual): a cuspidal pi of GL_n is paired nondegenerately with itself twisted by g -> transpose inverse (and conjugation on the compact factor); the global form of the theorem of Gelfand and Kazhdan [GK75] with strong multiplicity one [JS81b]. gal (UpperTheory.GalS.PairUAlt): as galoisRepOfPolarizedCuspidal for polarized pairs (PolarizedPair). car (UpperTheory.One.M.Row): the property of Definition gal-galois-representations. pur (ClozelPurity): purity for cuspidal pi on GL_a over a totally complex field whose infinitesimal character lies in Z + (a-1)/2, without regularity; same as [Clo90, Lemme 4.9]. chW (AlgebraicCharacterWD): as heckeLAdicParameterAbove with the local Artin map in place of rc; same in substance [Ser68; Fon94]. litN.coh (LitCoh): pt (PoitouTateNormalised): for l odd or F totally complex, the nine-term Poitou-Tate sequence with normalised local invariants, finiteness and duality of the Tate-Shafarevich groups, vanishing in degrees >= 3; same [NSW08, Chapter VIII]. lf, lt, le: local finiteness, Tate duality and the Euler characteristic formula (with the factor |M|^{[F_v:Q_l]} at v over l) for finite Z/l^r-modules at the finite places of a number field; same [NSW08, Chapter VII]. gf, ge: global finiteness (vanishing in degrees >= 3 for l odd) and Tate's global Euler characteristic formula for G_S with S containing the places over l; same [NSW08, Chapter VIII]. uo: at v not over l and M unramified, the unramified classes of M and of its twisted dual are exact annihilators; same [NSW08, Chapter VII]. gw: the Greenberg-Wiles formula for Selmer groups, l odd; same [Wil95, Proposition 1.6]. lfK, ltK, leK: the local statements over finite extensions of Q_l; same [NSW08, Chapter VII]. bk (BlochKatoLocal): the dimension formula for H^1_f of de Rham representations and the rational and integral orthogonality of H^1_f under local duality; same [BK90, Section 3]. litN.join (JoinOut): ToricDenominator, LatticeNormTransport.Transport, ToricTransport.TwistedTransport, ZetaValueIdeals.ZetaDenominators and SqTop.Refl. These are statements formulated for the proof, not published theorems. ToricDenominator bounds the l-adic valuations of normalised lattice sums of CM type by valuations of partial zeta values of the class group; Transport is a form of Shimura's reciprocity law for j-invariants and lattices of an imaginary quadratic field [Shi71, Chapter 5], with an equidistribution count and the Galois action on normalised lattice sums, whose algebraicity goes back to Damerell [Dam70]; TwistedTransport states algebraicity and Galois equivariance of twisted lattice sums divided by a period; ZetaDenominators bounds the denominators of partial zeta values zeta(C, 1-2s) of totally real fields (compare [DR80]); Refl is a reflection identity between Hecke L-values at integers with an algebraic unit factor. Same [MP94; MP96]. localFiniteness, localTateDuality, localEulerChar: as litN.coh.lf, lt, le.
lit-bundle-theta: published_results_first builds GlobalTheory.FunPr.ThetaLocalInputs, a structure with 53 Prop fields, without using the hypotheses of Remark lit-open-inputs. Fields of the same types as fields of UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses are compared in the note to Theorem lit-bundle-unitary: bernsteinUnitaryProductIrreducible, zelevinskyPolynomialRing, bernsteinZelevinskyFiniteness, cuspTraceClass, flathFactorisation, weilSiegelFormulaUnitary, doublingMethod, unramifiedDoublingGL, dixmierMalliavinFactorisation, schurOrthogonalitySquareIntegrable, strongApproxSU, harishChandraModules, discreteSeriesCover, formalDegreeCompactDual, discreteSeriesExists, harishChandraFinite, cuspRapidDecay, weilRepresentationUnitaryPair, discreteSeriesCoverExists and casselmanWallach. The others, with the same conventions: greenSeriesSt: GreenSeriesSt and BadShare.IsSeries: a map tau from monic squarefree polynomials f of degree N over F_g with nonzero constant term (sqSet) to class functions, injective, with each tau(f) the character of a simple generic representation of degree prod_{i=1}^N (g^i - 1) / |T_f|, where |T_f| = prod (g^d - 1) over the degrees d of the irreducible factors of f (torusCard). Weaker than Green's parametrisation of the irreducible characters [Gre55]: only these characters are given, without their values and without exhaustion. linnik: Theorem lit-linnik. complexMultiplicationJSt: for K imaginary quadratic, a Hilbert class field H with Artin isomorphism from the class group, H = K(j(a)) for every fractional ideal a, and art(b) j(a) = j(b^{-1} a). Same as the main theorem of complex multiplication for j-invariants [Sil94, Theorem II.4.3; Shi71, Chapter 5]. cuspidalMirabolic: CuspidalExists and CuspidalRestrictsToInduced, over finite fields: GL_{n+1}(k) has an irreducible cuspidal representation for every finite field k, and the restriction of an irreducible cuspidal representation to the mirabolic subgroup is the representation induced from a nontrivial character of the unipotent radical. Same [Gel70; Zel81]. weylBranching: the restriction of the irreducible representation of GL_N(C), and of U(N), of highest weight lam to GL_{N-1}(C), and to U(N-1), is the sum, with multiplicity one, of the representations whose highest weights interlace with lam. Same as Weyl's branching law [GW09, Chapter 8]. rallisInnerProductConvergent: RallisInnerProductConvergent, proved by rallis_of_dm from the doubling entry of Theorem lit-doubling. For rk A < rk B <= 2 rk A in Weil's convergent range, an irreducible cuspidal subrepresentation U of the cuspidal spectrum of U(A) whose theta lifts to the smaller spaces of the Witt tower of B vanish (LowerLiftsZero), and theta functions Phi_1, Phi_2 whose doubled function delta(Phi_1, Phi_2) is K-finite: the theta lifts of f_1, f_2 in U converge and are square-integrable, and the doubling zeta integral of the flat section through the Siegel-Weil section of delta(Phi_1, Phi_2) has the value at s_0 = (rk B - rk A)/2 equal to the normalised Petersson product of the lifts (ZetaValueAt). Special case of the Rallis inner product formula [Ral84; Li92] in the convergent range; compare Theorem th-rallis-inner-product. hermitianLocalGlobal: over a nonarchimedean local field with 2 invertible, two nondegenerate Hermitian forms of the same rank for a quadratic extension are equivalent exactly when the quotient of their determinants is a norm; over a CM field, forms equivalent at all finite places of the totally real subfield and at all complex embeddings are equivalent. Same [Jac62; Lan36]. quadraticClassFieldTheory: for a quadratic extension L/K of number fields, multiplicativity of the local norm residue symbols, the Hasse norm theorem, the exact sequence for almost everywhere norms, the product formula, and compatibility of the symbols with norms in a base change. Same as the quadratic case of class field theory [Neu99, Chapter VI]. borelCasselman: for admissible representations of GL_n(k), the projection from Iwahori invariants to the invariants of the integral torus in the Jacquet module for the Borel subgroup is bijective. Same [Bor76]. radfordShufflePolynomial: same [Rad79], over fields of characteristic 0. heckeLPartialContinuation: for a finite set T of places and a unitary Hecke character other than |.|^{it}, the partial L-function continues to an entire function without zeros on Re s >= 1, and (s-1) zeta^T(s) continues to an entire function without zeros on Re s >= 1. Same [Hec20; Tat67; Lan94, Chapter XV]. logDerOne: Mem.An.LogDerOne: |L'/L(1,chi) - sum 1/(1-rho)| <= C log(3q) for primitive chi mod q > 1, the sum over zeros with 0 < Re rho < 1 and |Im rho| <= 1 counted with multiplicity (zsum, zerosIn). Same as the estimate L'/L(s,chi) = sum_{|t - gamma| < 1} 1/(s - rho) + O(log q(|t|+2)) of [Dav00, Chapter 16] at s = 1; the zeros with |gamma| = 1 change the sum by O(log q). kFiniteVectorsUnitary: an irreducible unitary representation of U(J) is admissible, its K-finite vectors have analytic orbit maps, are dense, and form an irreducible module for the Lie algebra. Same [HC53]. discreteSeriesLowestKType: a discrete series representation with parameter lam contains the K-type lam + rho_n - rho_c, and two with the same parameter are unitarily equivalent. Same [Sch75; HC66]. holomorphicDiscreteSeries: for lam in the holomorphic chamber, the K-types of the discrete series are lam + rho_n - rho_c plus nonnegative combinations of the roots of p^+, K-finite vectors are smooth, p^- kills the lowest K-type, and the K-finite vectors are generated from it by raising operators. Same as Harish-Chandra's description of the holomorphic discrete series [HC56]. gKGlobalisation: AdmissibleClosure (the closure of an admissible (g,K)-submodule of a unitary representation is G-stable with K-finite part the submodule) and InfinitesimalEquivalence (irreducible unitary representations with isomorphic Harish-Chandra modules are unitarily equivalent, by an isometry proportional to the given isomorphism). Same [HC53]. cuspBounded, cuspDecayBound, cuspDecaySobolev: boundedness of cusp forms with all their derivatives, and two forms of uniform rapid decay with constants depending only on the open subgroup of invariance, the growth exponent and finitely many derivatives. Same in substance as the estimates of [HC68; MW95, Chapter I], for the unitary groups of a definite-side datum. heckeLEntireAndNonzeroAtOne: for unitary chi not of the form |.|^{it}, L(s,chi) continues to an entire function, and for chi nontrivial it is analytic and nonzero at s = 1. Same [Hec20; Lan94, Chapter XV]. realMetaplecticRepresentation, metaplecticRepresentation: the metaplectic double cover of Sp_{2l}(R) with the Weil representation on L^2(R^l), preserving the Schwartz space, intertwining the Heisenberg action, smooth with derivatives given by the quadratic operators, and with the Gaussian an eigenvector of the maximal compact subgroup. Same [Wei64]. gLHoweDuality: the polynomials on n x n' matrices decompose under GL_n(C) x GL_{n'}(C), and under U(n) x U(n'), as the sum over partitions with at most min(n,n') parts of tensor products of irreducibles, pairwise distinct on each side. Same [How89b]. kudlaSplittingSplitUnitary: for a Hermitian space alpha over a quadratic extension E/F of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic 0 and the split unitary group U(nu,nu), a smooth representation on Schwartz functions on alpha x nu matrices, unitary for L^2, intertwining the Heisenberg action, with the Siegel Levi acting by chi(det a) |N det a|^{dim alpha / 2} phi(x a). Same as Kudla's splitting in the Schroedinger model [Kud94]. idealInvariantsOneOrbitSt: j(a) is algebraic and its orbit under Aut(C/K) is the set of j(b), b a fractional ideal. Same [Sil94, Chapter II]. hermitianHassePrinciple: Hermitian forms over a quadratic extension of number fields that are equivalent at every place are equivalent. Same [Lan36]. stoneVonNeumann: over a nonarchimedean local field with 2 invertible, the Heisenberg group of a symplectic space has, for each nontrivial character psi, an irreducible smooth representation with central character psi, unique up to isomorphism. Same [MVW87, Chapitre 2]. discreteSeriesUpqExists: the type of discreteSeriesExists. thetaRationalInvariance: for the explicit model of theta functions attached to a CM elliptic curve (Crv, TT, WeilO; not unfolded), the operators of rational elements act on theta functions by an explicit factor prod_tau det^{-a_tau}. Related to Weil's invariance of theta distributions under rational points [Wei64]; formulated for that model and not compared. discreteSeriesHermitianUnique: discrete series of conjugate forms U(J) with the same parameter are unitarily equivalent after conjugation. Same [HC66]. siegelSetUnitary: for a unitary group of a Hermitian form over a CM extension and a Witt basis: an Iwasawa decomposition, a closed Siegel set covering the adelic quotient, the Siegel property and the integration bound, the comparison of heights under rational elements, and rapid decay of cusp forms on the Siegel set. Same as reduction theory for these groups [Bor69; BHC62], with rapid decay [MW95, Chapter I]. weilRepresentationExists: the existence of the global Weil representation of a Hermitian and a skew-Hermitian space over a CM extension with Hecke characters, in a second explicit model (Model.IsWeil, not unfolded). Same in substance as [Kud94; HKS96]. howeDualityReal: Theorem lit-howe-duality-real.
lit-casselman-wallach: A special case of the Casselman-Wallach theorem [Cas89; Wal92, Chapter 11]. The group is U(J) for the diagonal sign matrix Jm(eps), with K = Kset(eps) and Lie algebra lieSet(eps), and the source is the space of smooth vectors (SmoothVec) of an irreducible unitary representation (IsURepOn, IsIrredOn); the published theorem applies to every Harish-Chandra module of a real reductive group and its smooth Frechet globalisation of moderate growth. The hypotheses on the target (IsSmoothModRep: countably many seminorms, continuous action, derivatives of every vector, moderate growth for 1+sum|g_ab|^2) are the published ones. T is a linear map on all of H, constrained only on smooth vectors; its continuity is the Sobolev bound IsSmoothGMap, and part (4), the reverse Sobolev bound, says that T is a topological embedding with closed image.
lit-howe-duality-real: Weaker than Howe's theorem [How89]. ThetaSubInf N, a theta subspace in the text, says that N lies in the Fock space M.Pol, contains the derivatives of the action of continuous one-parameter subgroups of U(X)(F_inf) (Lines) and the differences omega(k)f - f for k in KInf, and is stable under Lines and KInf of U(W). Parts (1) and (2) state that the quotient of the Fock space by the smallest such N, the big theta lift of the trivial representation, has finite length and a unique maximal proper submodule. Howe's theorem asserts this for every irreducible (u(X),K_X)-module occurring as a quotient of the Fock space, and that the resulting correspondence is injective; only the trivial representation is treated, and injectivity is not stated. The statement is for the product over all archimedean places at once. Model also carries Darboux coordinates, vacuum vectors and a fundamental domain, which do not enter the conclusion.
lit-green-cuspidal: The same as Green's theorem on cuspidal characters [Gre55]. IsCusp asks that the class function be an irreducible character (IsIrr) and that res a (d-a) chi 1 1 = 0 for 0 < a < d; res a b chi 1 1 is the average of chi over the unipotent radical of the parabolic of type (a,b), which is the dimension of the invariants, so this is the cuspidality condition of the text. The map tau is defined on all characters of K^x, but only its values at regular characters are constrained.
lit-labelling: LabelDatum: teich is a monoid homomorphism from Fbar_g to C that is injective on nonzero elements, and gen d has order g^d - 1 with the stated norm compatibility. thetaOf L d x z is teich(x)^n when z = (gen d)^n and 0 otherwise; on F_{g^d}^x it is theta_{x,d}.
lit-green-labelled: green_of_regular deduces GlobalTheory.GLq.Green, which is GlobalTheory.Published.GreenCuspidal, from Theorem lit-green-cuspidal applied to the field KK g d. The proof in the text follows it: regularity of theta_{x,d} for a root x of P (regular_iff), the character formula through an embedding of the splitting field of the characteristic polynomial (exists_emb_eq, sum_range_eq_roots), injectivity from injectivity of the labelling, and surjectivity through minimal polynomials. IsCuspOf L P chi requires the character formula for every root x of P (rootsBar P).
lit-weil-datum: IsThetaFunO and IsWeilDatumO in Formalism.IndefR.Datum. WO S T is Mx D T.rank S.rank, matrices over A_E; the symplectic form is symplO (the trace of xi0 times a Hermitian pairing built from the inverse Gram matrix of S and the Gram matrix of T), and heisO uses half of it. The conditions on omega are om_pres, om_heis, om_aut, om_cont, om_unit and om_split; the last says that on split idempotent components omega(g,h) multiplies Heisenberg-invariant functionals by a positive constant times chi_T(x)^{-1} chi_S(y) for determinants x, y, which the text paraphrases. psi satisfies IsStdChar D psi (-1): a character of A_F/F with archimedean component exp(-2 pi i sum_rho theta_rho(x)), the sum over a CM type. The restriction conditions are ResEta D chi n.
lit-siegel-eisenstein: degPS V a mu s is degPSOf, the space indSpace of continuous right K-finite functions with the law IndLaw: Phi(p g) = mu(det a(p)) |det a(p)|^{s + n/2} Phi(g), where a(p) is the Levi component (leviOf, the action on the diagonal) and |.| is absE, the product over all places of the normalized absolute value of the norm to F (absEv, absEw). Since the modulus character of the Siegel parabolic of U(n,n) is |det a|^n, I(s,mu) is the normalized induction of mu |det|^s, so that Re s = 0 is the unitary axis. flat V a phi s1 s is flatSec: phi(g) times iwAbs(g)^{s - s1}, with iwAbs(pk) = |det a(p)| for the decomposition G = P K_a; this is well defined because |det a| is trivial on the compact group P intersected with K_a. K_a is Khat V a = KAd of the doubled Gram matrix, with the lattice frameLat V twice and the archimedean majorant (a, a). IsMaj and HasIwasawa (the decomposition G = P K_a) are hypotheses of the theorems that use the definition; the text puts the second in the definition. eis V Phi is the coset sum over P(F)\G(F); left invariance under P(F) and absolute convergence for Re s > n/2 (IsEisFamily) are conclusions of the theorems below.
lit-weil-siegel: The same as Weil's results in this range [Wei65]: his convergence criterion for theta integrals (B anisotropic or rk A + r_B < rk B) and the Siegel-Weil formula where the Eisenstein series converges absolutely (2 rk A < rk B). In part (1) the seminorm is IsContSeminorm, continuity in the archimedean Schwartz component for each fixed finite component, applied to phi composed with the coordinates coord. Parts (2) and (3) are for Weil data on the doubled space A^box and B with trivial character on A^box. The Siegel-Weil section is integrated over a fundamental domain in the model of quasi-periodic functions; this corresponds to the partial Fourier transform at zero in a Schrödinger model.
lit-siegel-weil: A special case of the Siegel-Weil formula for unitary groups in Weil's convergent range [Ich04; Ich07], the unitary analogue of [KR88] for orthogonal groups: the theta integral converges, but rk B <= 2 rk A puts s0 = (rk B - rk A)/2 outside the range of absolute convergence of the Eisenstein series. The statement is restricted to rk A < rk B and to Fock vectors (IsFockVec: theta functions annihilated by long enough products of archimedean annihilation operators for the complex structures of the Cartan involutions), with the flat section through the Siegel-Weil section at s0 and a covolume-one measure. EisValueAt asks for an analytic continuation near s0 with the stated value; the right side is the average over [U(B)] for the probability measure.
lit-doubling: ResidueKilled.DM, which is the content of the field named DoublingMethodLocalZetaIntegrals. Despite the name it says nothing about local zeta integrals (convergence, unramified computation or nonvanishing); the unramified computation for GL is the separate entry UnramifiedDoublingGL. It states the global basic identity of the doubling method [GPSR87, Part A] (BasicIdentity: DblConv, ZetaConvH and dblInt = zetaH with the Petersson coefficient petCoef) and the meromorphic continuation of the Siegel Eisenstein series (part (1), which is GlobalTheory.Published.SiegelEisensteinContinuation) and of the doubling integral (ZetaContinues). Its middle conjunct is True. The corresponding conjunct of GlobalTheory.Published.DoublingMethod, a simple pole at (b-n)/2 when n < b, is not proved (Remark lit-vacuous-slot). ResidueKilled.dm_of_two proves DM from CuspRapidDecay and SiegelEisensteinContinuation; its third argument has type True and is supplied as trivial. Part (2) is for f1, f2 in Cusp.A0 theta V A with IsCartanFrame V A and V.SigOK.
lit-vacuous-slot: GlobalTheory.Published.UnusedSlot72 is defined as True, and siegel_eisenstein_simple_pole is proved by trivial; the field it fills in UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses is named siegelEisensteinSimplePole. The real statement is GlobalTheory.Published.SiegelEisensteinSimplePole, a conjunct of GlobalTheory.Published.DoublingMethod and a field of several other hypothesis bundles; neither is proved on the path to the main theorems. ResidueKilled.DM is DoublingMethod with that conjunct replaced by True.
lit-jacquet-shalika: A special case of the results of Jacquet and Shalika [JS81a; JS81b], for E totally complex. Part (1) is JacquetShalikaRigidity, the classification of isobaric sums by their Satake parameters at almost all places, for families in CG E a (isomorphism classes of irreducible cuspidal subspaces) and without a unitarity hypothesis; the plan described it for unitary representations. Part (2) is JacquetShalikaBound, for representations with unitary central character (CG.IsUnitary). HasSat w B says that the local component at w is unramified with Satake multiset B.
lit-clozel-cohomological: The same as Clozel's lemma [Clo90, Lemme 3.14], for E totally complex. Regular algebraic is CG.IsRegAlg (isRegAlg_iff: distinct exponents in Z + (a-1)/2 at every embedding). GKCoh.IsCohomological asks for an irreducible algebraic representation Xi of GL_a(E tensor C) such that the relative Lie algebra complex of pi_inf tensor Xi, with cochains on Hermitian matrices equivariant for K_inf, has nonzero cohomology in some degree.
lit-bhatt-scholze: The same as the main theorem of Bhatt and Scholze [BS23], in the form of essential surjectivity onto lattices in crystalline representations with coefficients in O_L, together with full faithfulness of the realisation evaluated at the A_inf-prism. Realises asks for a semilinear map j over A_inf -> W(C^flat) that is a base change isomorphism (SemiBC), compatible with Frobenius after inverting an element of the prism ideal, and Galois-equivariant. Crystallinity is IsCrys with respect to period ring data P.PD K satisfying IsStd. The Lean proves it from the integral form BhattScholzeIntegral (bhattScholze_coeff).
lit-hodge-tate-sequence: Weaker than Fargues's theorem on the Hodge-Tate sequence of a p-divisible group over O_C [Far08]. Only the duality in the middle of the sequence is stated: the kernel of alpha_G is the orthogonal of the kernel of alpha_{G dual} under the Weil pairing. Surjectivity of alpha_G after inverting p, the bound on its cokernel, and the identification of its kernel with Lie(G) tensor O(1) are not stated. hodgeTateLinear G is dlogLinear of the dual composed with the bidual isomorphism. B is any O-bilinear form that agrees on Tate modules with the Weil pairing read through the trivialisation of T_p(mu) given by zeta.
lit-linnik: The same as Linnik's theorem [Lin44]. leastPrimeMod a q is the infimum of the set of primes congruent to a mod q, which would be 0 if that set were empty; linnik_iff_exists_prime shows, with Dirichlet's theorem from Mathlib, that the statement is equivalent to the existence of a prime p congruent to a mod q with p <= C q^L.
lit-chebotarev-degree-one: The qualitative form of the Chebotarev density theorem [Che26; Neu99, Chapter VII, Section 13]: one place outside S, of absolute residue degree one (inertiaDeg over Z equal to 1), unramified in L (inertia group contained in the fixing subgroup of L), with a Frobenius element (IsFrob for the norm of v) restricting to g. The published theorem gives the density of such places, from which this follows.
lit-snc-sequence: IsSncBlowupSeq g E s E': each step blows up Z (FinalTheorems.Blowup, the universal property of the blow-up) on X_i smooth over k, with Z smooth over k and IsSncCentre E_i Z, and replaces E_i by totalTransform, the preimage of E_i union the support of Z. FinalTheorems.Snc and SncAt are the simple normal crossings condition of the text.
lit-principalization: Weaker than principalization in the form of Hironaka [Hir64, Main Theorem II] and Kollár [Kol07, Theorem 35]. The published theorem makes the total transform of I the ideal of a divisor that has simple normal crossings jointly with the transformed boundary. The Lean asks that I O_X' be invertible (EffCartier) and its reduced zero set be simple normal crossings, and separately that the sequence be a normal crossings blow-up sequence starting from E; it does not state that the zero set of I O_X' together with the transform E' of E has simple normal crossings. The isomorphism over the complement of the zero set of I is stated; that the centres lie over that zero set is not. For E empty the case is in the Hironaka book of Resolution [Res26, Tag R021].
lit-principalization-projective: GlobalTheory.Published.Principalisation, deduced by principalisation_closed (through principalisation_of_charZero) from Theorem lit-principalization with E empty, as in the proof. The replacement of centres is CentreOver.exists_centre_off and seq_of_iso. Since s is an isomorphism off the zero set of I, the exceptional divisors lie in the reduced zero set of I O_Y', which is simple normal crossings; so this corollary is the usual principalization for an ideal on a smooth projective variety with empty boundary [Hir64; Kol07, Theorem 35; Res26, Tag R021].
lit-resolution: A corollary of Theorem cv-functorial-resolution: resolutionCharZero_of_top extracts existence, smoothness, the isomorphism over the smooth locus and the simple normal crossings condition (on preRed, the reduced inverse image of the non-smooth locus). The sequence is an arbitrary finite sequence of blow-ups (IsBlowupSeq, with no condition on the centres). Compared with [Kol07, Theorem 36] and [Hir64, Main Theorem I], the conditions on the centres and functoriality are dropped. The Hironaka book of Resolution proves the existence of such a sequence for integral X, without the normal crossings condition [Res26, Tag R02G].
lit-arithmetic-variety: IsArithVar p D: k a domain finite over Z, X integral, projective (IsProjOver) and flat over Spec k, of Krull dimension D+1. HermLB: a line bundle with a weight phi_sigma for each sigma: k -> C, smooth (IsCInf) and compatible with conjugation. HermLB.IsNef: SemiPos D, nonnegative self-intersection on vertical integral curves over finite fields, nonnegative curve degree on horizontal integral curves. smallSec: sections with pointwise norm at most 1 at every complex point. SemiPos was not unfolded beyond its name.
lit-arithmetic-hilbert-samuel: GlobalTheory.Published.ArithHilbertSamuel. The self-intersection a enters through IsSelfInter a: the value at the generic point of an arithmetic height function for L-bar. It is proved from Corollary lit-principalization-projective by arithHilbertSamuel_of_principalisation, through the ample case and a pullback of semipositive metrics. Its form matches the arithmetic Hilbert-Samuel formula for nef Hermitian line bundles [GS92; Zha95; Mor09]; the published hypotheses (for instance on the generic fibre) were not compared in detail.
lit-hilbert-samuel-upper: PositivityTheory.MbHsUse.HSUse is ArithKleiman.Statement (part (1)), G7.Statement (part (2)) and ArithmeticVolumeNef.Statement = ArithmeticHilbertSamuelUpperBound (part (3)), in the setting of Definition lit-multiprojective; it is a hypothesis of Theorem cv-covolume-bound-from-literature and is proved by hsUse_outright. Part (2) also asks that the generic degree genDeg (the mixed multiplicity intNum over Q of P with D copies of a) be positive, and generation is KH.GeneratesOn. Part (3) has no characteristic hypothesis on Omega; horizontality of P forces characteristic 0. Part (1) is the nonnegativity of the self-intersection of a nef metrized line bundle [Zha95; Mor09], here for the restriction of O(a) with a smooth metric to a subvariety of a product of projective spaces; a special case. Parts (2) and (3) are weaker than the arithmetic Hilbert-Samuel formula for nef bundles [Zha95; Mor09], which gives the limit and its value: only the upper bound for the limsup is stated, in (2) for bundles generated by finitely many small sections and in (3) for bundles whose monomial sections are small, with sections counted on the normalization. In both cases the bundle is nef, so the published theorem applies.
lit-zarhin: Weaker than Zarhin's trick [Zar74; MB85, Chapitre IX]: the published statement shows that (A x A dual)^4 is principally polarized, which contains A as a direct factor. The Lean states only that A is a retract of some principally polarized abelian scheme, and only over the valuation ring of an algebraically closed valued field. It is proved from duality of abelian schemes (DualAbelianScheme) and the theorem of the cube.
lit-multiprojective: The objects of ReciprocityTheory.ChartRestriction.G.Geo used by the statements of Proposition lit-hilbert-samuel-upper. R is MRing = MvPolynomial (Sigma k, iota k) Z; the points of X-hat(C) are mcPts. IsArithVar P d: K nonempty, P prime, multihomogeneous and relevant (IsMultiProjPrime), horizontal (P meets Z in 0) and Krull dimension of R/P equal to d + |K|. HermLine is the pair (a, h) with h positive and homogeneous of multidegree a; smoothness is IsSmoothHerm. IsSemipositiveRel P0 P A asks for the Levi form of log h on the vectors tangent to the cone of P0 at points of X(C), for some P0 contained in P; since the theorems hold for every such P0 and P0 = P gives the weakest condition, the text states the case P0 = P. NefOnFibres uses geoNum 1 W a on the vertical curves W containing P. An intersection system II is any function satisfying IsIntersectionFamily for all K and iota: symmetry, additivity in the last argument for the tensor product of metrized line bundles, and the recursion recR, whose terms are the multiplicities multAt over the relevant minimal primes of P + (s) (divSupp), II on horizontal components, geoNum times log of the characteristic (charOf) on vertical ones, and arInt, the integral of log(|s|/h) against the Monge-Ampere densities of the log h_j computed through a projection (ptsIntegral; the normalisation of maDensity was not unfolded). These are the axioms of the inductive definition of heights of Bost, Gillet and Soule; uniqueness of II is not stated. The function field condition is Birational y, with P = mCoordIdeal y; H^0 and its normalized version are chartLat and chartLatNm, intersections over the charts chartRingZ y c; smallness is IsSmallH and the count is smallSectionCount, the logarithm of the number of small elements.
